chunks: Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, from his father, from his grandfather عليهم السلام, who said:
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, ṣalawātu llāhi ʿalayhi, said: “Do not say: ‘Ramaḍān’; rather say: ‘Shahr Ramaḍān,’ for you do not know what Ramaḍān is.”

key_terms.رَمَضَانُ: Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the fuller and more reverential expression
key_terms.لَا تَدْرُونَ: you do not know; indicating the hidden significance of the term
key_terms.لَا تَقُولُوا: do not say; a direct prohibition of a form of speech

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام instruct believers to say “Shahr Ramaḍān” instead of just “Ramaḍān”?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches proper reverential wording regarding the blessed month of fasting. It instructs believers to say “the Month of Ramadan” rather than merely “Ramadan,” indicating respect for the sacredness and deeper reality associated with this month.
